title.narrative: Strengthened constituent capacity to promote enabling environments for sustainable enterprise development, decent work and productivity growth.

description.narrative: South Africa’s employment creation and economic growth strategy places sustainable micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) at its centre. However, many enterprises face low productivity, weak business management practices, limited access to markets and finance, and significant decent work deficits that constrain growth, formalization and competitiveness. Enterprises are also under increasing pressure to comply with labour standards, responsible business conduct and environmental sustainability requirements while adapting to economic, technological and climate transitions. The ILO supports the design, implementation and monitoring of integrated policies and frameworks that promote sustainable enterprise development, productivity growth and decent work. Support is also directed towards strengthening entrepreneurship and innovation, improving access to business development and financial services for MSMEs, and promoting responsible business conduct and due diligence grounded in international labour standards, including through social dialogue processes and supply chain interventions. The programme also supports constituents to design and operationalize coherent just transition policies and programmes that integrate decent work into climate and development strategies. The outcome benefits MSMEs, entrepreneurs and workers, particularly those affected by low productivity, informality and transition pressures, as well as government departments and institutions, employers’ and workers’ organizations, productivity bodies, enterprise development support institutions, and national and sectoral social dialogue platforms at national and sub-national levels. The strategy is implemented in partnership with government, employers’ and workers’ organizations, productivity and enterprise development institutions, social dialogue platforms, and the broader UN system to promote coordinated action, policy coherence and measurable improvements in decent work outcomes.
